title: Release 1.0.18: the Workshop, where JARVIS does things himself
summary: JARVIS has a workshop: his own folder on this PC where he reads, writes and deletes files (a replaced or deleted file goes to the workshop's recycle folder first), runs commands and reads their exit code, output and errors, keeps his own Python environment for the packages a job needs (made once from the PC's own Python; nothing is ever installed into JARVIS's own), and remembers lessons from one job to the next. On a goal with several steps he runs a mission: "Jarvis, start a mission: write a script that lists the ten largest files in the workshop and make it run." He writes a plan, does the steps one by one, reads every result, fixes what fails and runs it again until the exit code is 0, within a time limit (Settings > Workshop, 15 minutes by default) and 60 tool calls, then tells you (a notice on the PC and the phone); the mission's own chat holds the plan, every step and the result, and Settings > Workshop shows the missions, lets you start or stop one, add other folders JARVIS may use, and read or delete the lessons. Every tool a mission uses obeys its switch in Settings > Permissions (five new rows: files, commands, the Python environment, lessons, missions; commands ship as "ask first", so you approve each one on the PC before it runs, and you set that switch to Allowed for a mission to run commands unattended), keys and passwords are kept out of every command and its output, nothing is reachable outside the workshop and the folders you add, and the emergency stop ends a mission and its running command at once. Built on the owner's words of 2026-10-07: file system operations, terminal access, goal decomposition and planning, self-correction, short-term and long-term memory (docs/WORKSHOP.md). Also for the phone: a paired device may now read the list of this Core's devices (your paired devices with what you allow each, this PC with its JARVIS version, the test client marked as simulated), which the iPhone app's device panel shows; read only, nothing on it can be changed from a device (docs/PHONE-DEVICES-1.0.18.md). And two fixes from the phone's checks: when JARVIS sets a timer he names the time it goes off on this PC's clock (he no longer works the time out himself; one reply said 07:19 for a timer due at 10:29), and "remember that" saves your own last line, while "remember what you said" saves JARVIS's last answer (docs/CORE-FIXES-20261010.md).
validation: Development suites passed at the release commit (the counts are recorded in the README of this release's checks). The Workshop had one independent review whose findings were applied (docs/WORKSHOP.md). test_workshop.py runs real cmd.exe commands and the test Python in a temporary workshop: the recycle folder, nothing outside the allowed folders, the same-mistake guard, the time limit and the stop, keys out of the environment and the output, the mission loop with a fake model (a real SyntaxError fed back and fixed), and the whole path through a local Core (the switches "off" and "ask first", a mission from the panel, the emergency stop). Not tested: a real provider driving a mission.

title: Release 1.0.17: JARVIS as his own app, and everything JARVIS said he could not do
summary: JARVIS is now his own program. The release ships JARVIS.exe (Electron renamed and stamped with the Teague Industries badge, the name JARVIS, the company and the version), so Task Manager, the taskbar, the window, the tray and notifications all say JARVIS; a double-click on JARVIS.exe opens JARVIS; the Desktop and Startup shortcuts point straight at it (also after a rollback), and the old PowerShell launcher is no longer written for this release. The app works out its own folders from where it is installed, and an old pin that still points at a previous release's JARVIS.exe hands the start over to the current one. The release comes as one file, JARVIS-Setup-1.0.17-<commit>.exe: double-click, Next, done. It installs for your user account only (no administrator rights), updates an installed JARVIS the same way (the previous release kept as the rollback copy; your data, keys and preferences untouched), reinstalls, and registers JARVIS 1.0.17, Teague Industries in Settings > Apps > Installed apps, whose Uninstall removes the program and keeps your data. Inside it runs the same install engine every earlier release passed; the zip with install.cmd still exists and still works. The Stage 7 check learned the new shape (version 4 scripts: install from the Setup, the Installed-apps entry, uninstall through it, one update through the Setup). Three fixes from the phone checks: replies are streamed to a paired device while they are written when the PC's setting Show replies while they are written is on and the provider is Qwen; "remember that" saves the line before it instead of the word that; and the action guard appends the truth under a reply instead of replacing it. Two music items: the music can be stopped again (in 1.0.16 a song opened by one request could not be seen, paused or stopped by the next, because Windows ties a song to the thread that opened it, so "stop music" answered "Nothing was playing" while the song played on; every media command now goes through one thread of JARVIS's own), and a start-up song: in Settings > Music choose the song JARVIS plays once he has said his greeting at a sign-in start (nothing by default). Everything JARVIS said he was not allowed to do (docs/PHONE-ACCESS-PLAN.md), each off until you switch it on: two ticks per paired device in Settings > Devices, May use this PC's tools (the device's questions get the same tools as the PC's, under your Permissions switches) and May approve for JARVIS (an Ask-first call or a mail draft can be approved or refused from the phone; a waiting approval lives fifteen minutes); screen analysis from the phone (the PC window's capture described once and kept nowhere); location with a question (used for that answer only, stored nowhere); Gmail and Google Calendar through three lines in the key file (an app password and the calendar's secret address; the tools mail_search, mail_read and calendar_events, mail_send always asks first; Settings > Connections > Connectors with a TEST for each; the daily briefing gains a calendar section); every saved memory, note, task and project carries the release it was saved under, and when two facts about JARVIS himself disagree the newer release wins while the older stays saved; Settings > Routine holds your week as blocks, and JARVIS raises one nudge when a task or reminder collides with a block about to start (none in quiet hours or while stopped), shows notices as toasts, lists them to paired devices and speaks them on this PC in his voice when you allow it, never reading out words that carry the wake word or a stop phrase near his own microphone; a paired device can ask the PC to announce a text; and Settings > Devices > On this network lists the devices Windows has seen on your home network, read only when you ask, named through your own DNS server only, with the tool network_devices. 51 tools now, each with its own switch in Settings > Permissions. A rollback to 1.0.16 keeps your data (the new tables and columns are left alone) but knows none of this: no device ticks, no mail, calendar, routine, notices or network list, no streamed replies to the phone, and its shortcuts and launcher come back as they were; the Installed-apps entry stays and still uninstalls the program with the data kept.
validation: Development suites passed at the release commit (the counts are recorded in docs/release-rehearsal-20261007-1017/README.md). Every part had one independent review whose findings were applied: the own-app items 3.1 to 3.3, the Setup with the version 4 Stage 7 scripts, the shortcut fix of 2026-10-07, the three phone-check fixes, and the access items A, C and D, G, E, F and H (docs/OWN-APP-1.0.17.md, docs/PHONE-CORE-FIXES-20261007.md, docs/PHONE-ACCESS-1.0.17.md). The Setup was rehearsed in a sandbox on this PC with the owner's real Desktop and Startup shortcuts recorded before and after every step and required unchanged (an earlier rehearsal, before the fix, had rewritten and then removed them). The built package goes through the release regression, a zip install, that Setup rehearsal and a local Stage 7 pass with the version 4 scripts (install from the Setup, Installed-apps entry, uninstall through it, update, rollback, update again, one update through the Setup, the interrupted update). Not tested in this entry: the check in the test VM (Stage 7) and the update of the everyday JARVIS, which follow on the owner's approvals; Gmail and the calendar against real accounts (the owner's steps in docs/GOOGLE-STEPS.md); the phone's half of each access item (built on the Mac); the Nest camera (not built: it waits for the owner's Device Access steps).

title: Release 1.0.16: the phone release
summary: The PC side of the iPhone app (docs/PHONE-PLAN.md), and nothing else. A new switch in Settings > Devices, Private network, off until you turn it on: with it on, and Tailscale running and signed in on this PC, JARVIS opens a second door at this PC's Tailscale address, on a port you choose (8790 unless you change it), for paired devices only. Through that door only the device routes are served, each request with the device's own key; your settings, keys, pages and RESUME stay on this PC, and JARVIS itself still listens on this PC's own address exactly as before. If Tailscale is not running the panel says so and nothing is open; the door opens by itself when Tailscale comes up and closes at once when the switch goes off. Pairing limits for a JARVIS that can be reached: wrong codes and wrong keys are counted per caller, and a caller that tries too many is locked out for fifteen minutes while your pairing keeps waiting for the right device. A paired device can now read its own conversations, the PC's health as the dashboard shows it (nothing new is measured), and an overview of your open tasks, projects and the next day's reminders; its answer route waits for news instead of being asked every tenth of a second; and a recording from a device is refused while the emergency stop holds. A tick per device, May save memories and tasks, off for every new device: with it, your own phone can save a memory, a note, a task or a timer under the same switches as the PC (a tool set to Ask first asks on the PC); everything else a device cannot change stays as it was. Music from your own files (Settings > Music): copy MP3 files into the music folder JARVIS shows you, give a song a nickname, and say "Jarvis, play workshop warrior"; "stop the music", "pause", "resume", "volume up", "volume down" and "what is playing" work the same way, answered by JARVIS itself with no AI in the loop and played on this PC's speakers whether the window is open or not; the tool "Play music from your files" has its own switch in Settings > Permissions, and the emergency stop stops the music too. The Qwen cloned voice now speaks: Alibaba hands out the finished sound as a plain http link on its own file server, which JARVIS refused until now; the sound is now fetched over https from that same Alibaba server, and nothing else is accepted. A rollback to 1.0.15 keeps every paired device and your nickname list but knows neither the switch (the door stays closed), nor the tick (devices only read), nor the music commands, and its Qwen voice does not speak.
validation: Development suites passed at the release commit: 664 Python tests, 52 desktop tests, 18 Intelligence tests and 24 interface scripts. Each of the three parts (the phone release, the music and the voice link fix) had an independent review whose findings were applied. The private-network door was tested with a second loopback address standing in for the PC's Tailscale address; no real Tailscale network and no real phone were used, and the switch was never turned on outside the tests. The music player was tried once on this PC with a generated two-second tone and otherwise with a stand-in for Windows' media interface. The Qwen voice link rule was tested with stand-ins in the test suites; the owner-run check tool was given the same rule. The built package goes through the release regression, a zip install and a local Stage 7 rehearsal. Not tested in this entry: the check in the test VM (Stage 7) and the update of the everyday JARVIS, which follow on the owner's approvals and are recorded in docs/CURRENT-STATUS.md.

title: Release 1.0.15: the new look, permissions, devices, backups by themselves, answers offline
summary: A new look for the whole interface: one header with eight everyday sections and More, a dashboard built from real data only (system states, devices, performance, the day's schedule), and chat replies that show their formatting instead of raw marks. AI providers: JARVIS now uses OpenAI and Qwen only for thinking and pictures, and Fish Audio or the Qwen cloned voice for speech; Groq, Gemini and ElevenLabs are removed. If your key file says JARVIS_PROVIDER=groq or JARVIS_PROVIDER=gemini, change that line to openai or qwen, otherwise JARVIS says the provider is not supported. Answer speed for Qwen (Settings > AI): Deep thinks before every answer as before and stays the default, Auto answers quickly and thinks first when asked, Economy uses the cheaper fast model. Backup provider (on; a tick box in Settings > AI): when the chosen provider refuses or cannot be reached, the other one answers that question and the reply says so; never after a tool has already run in that question. Permissions in one place (Settings > Permissions): every tool is listed with what it does and can be switched off or set to ask first; an emergency stop that holds until you press RESUME on the PC, also across a restart; changes JARVIS makes to its own personality or style ask first. Devices (Settings > Devices): a device pairs with a code you read from the PC, gets a key of its own, may use only what you tick, and can be revoked at any time. JARVIS still listens on this PC only; nothing is opened to the network. Speech recognition (Settings > AI): on this PC as before, or by the chosen AI provider with this PC as the fallback. Automatic backups (Settings > Backups): off until you choose a folder, for example on a backup drive; then one a day or a week, each made and checked like a backup made by hand, old automatic ones thinned out, a backup made by hand never removed. Answers without the internet: when no AI provider can be reached and the program Ollama with a chat model is installed on this PC, that local model answers and the reply says so; it cannot use tools. On by default (it does nothing without Ollama); a tick box in Settings > AI switches it off. Replies that appear while they are written (Settings > AI, off by default, Qwen only): the answer appears sentence by sentence, and only what has passed the same checks as a finished answer is shown. Also: plain messages when a request is too large for a plan or a model is not activated; a real-size connection check in Settings > Developer; a provider request that carries a key is never sent on to another address; backups and the switch-over carry your own style sheet; the screen label sent with a screenshot reads correctly. If you roll back to 1.0.14: the older program does not know the emergency stop that holds, the tool switches, device keys or automatic backups, so none of them is enforced or runs there; your saved data is kept.
validation: Development suites passed at the release commit: 634 Python tests, 52 desktop tests, 18 Intelligence tests and 23 interface scripts. Every one of the eight new parts had an independent review whose findings were applied. The built package goes through the release regression, a zip install and a local Stage 7 rehearsal (install, restart check, uninstall and reinstall, update, rollback and an interrupted update). Not tested in this entry: the check in the test VM (Stage 7) and the update of the everyday JARVIS; and with the real providers: replies shown while written, speech recognition by Qwen, the Qwen cloned voice, the backup provider taking over, and a real loss of the internet. Those were tested with stand-ins on this PC; the local model was asked for real.

title: Release 1.0.14: fixes found during acceptance and the switch-over
summary: Checking or importing a backup on a read-only disc no longer waits forever: it is checked in this installation's backup folder or refused at once with a plain message. Update timings now separate re-checking an installed release from stopping JARVIS; the installer no longer waits 30 seconds for a Core that crashed, never ends its own process, and refuses to run with an installed release's Python. The desktop app closes quietly when JARVIS is stopped on purpose (another app, an update or an uninstall) and shows a message only after a crash. Settings > About shows the installed version. Provider refusals say which provider refused and tell a missing-credit or billing limit (waiting will not help, no pause) from a temporary rate limit. The default Gemini model is gemini-3.8-flash; a GEMINI_MODEL line in the key file still wins. Update, rollback and uninstall now wait until every JARVIS program has really exited, and refuse with a plain message, changing nothing, if one keeps running or the check itself fails; an uninstall removes the launcher first and waits briefly for a file still in use, so JARVIS is never left pointing at a half-removed release. "Quit JARVIS completely" now returns only when the background Core has really exited.
validation: Development suites passed at the release commit: 373 Python tests, 52 desktop tests, 18 Intelligence tests and 17 interface scripts. The built package goes through the release regression, a zip install and a local Stage 7 rehearsal (install, restart check, uninstall and reinstall, update, rollback and an interrupted update). The check in the test VM (Stage 7), the update of the everyday JARVIS and live provider replies are not tested in this entry. 1.0.12 and 1.0.13 were built but never offered: the local Stage 7 rehearsal of 1.0.12 found the uninstall defect, and the release regression of 1.0.13 found that "Quit JARVIS completely" could return a moment before the Core had exited; both are fixed here.

title: Optional Gemini conversation provider
summary: Adds Gemini 2.5 Flash through Google's compatibility endpoint. Existing context, tools, evidence guards and voice settings are retained. Local masked setup tests a generic reply before saving the provider selection. No automatic provider fallback. Initial adapter waits for a complete response; streaming optimisation remains separate.
validation: 110 offline Python tests passed, including five Gemini adapter checks. Local setup imports passed. Live account access, tool use, answer quality, voice and latency have not yet been tested. Creating a key does not prove free-tier eligibility.

title: Persistent state-coloured hologram and voice latency profiling
summary: Adaptive hologram rail across workspaces; violet thinking, amber tool execution, teal transcription acceptance, red errors, breathing and subtle pointer parallax. Listening pill visually hidden with accessible status retained. In-memory development voice timing report and configurable endpoint waiting, default 1.28 seconds instead of 2.56. Existing provider, memory, personality and evidence guards retained.
validation: 105 Python tests passed and all 13 pages checked at five viewport sizes with no page errors or horizontal overflow. Deterministic PCM endpoint test: 2560 ms before, 1280 ms after. This is endpoint waiting only, not measured total voice latency. End-to-end live BEFORE/AFTER remains unmeasured; no early unchecked LLM speech or speculative STT calls introduced.

title: Audio-reactive holographic voice core
summary: Shared wire-sphere renderer for the main, compact and floating holograms. Actual playback samples drive the central waveform with RMS smoothing, frequency-band ring and particle response, and energy-rise pulses. Listening uses measured microphone level; thinking, processing, interruption and error transitions are distinct. Reduced motion and hidden-canvas drawing limits are respected. Existing audio providers and controls are retained.
validation: 105 Python tests and 13 desktop tests passed. Real Web Audio oscillator tests confirm loud/quiet response and smooth silence decay, with output muted. All 13 app pages rendered without JavaScript errors. Floating companion renderer loaded and processed sample fixtures. Configured-provider speech audibility and physical-device 60 FPS have not been measured. Browser speech synthesis has no accessible waveform and is not represented with invented audio.

title: Teague Industries visual system
summary: Shared navy surface, typography and spacing tokens across all 13 sections; compact persistent voice shell; contextual communications rail; real record counts; project cards and linked-record filters; memory search; task and mission-log filters; document display modes and inspector; session web searches; structured diagram canvas; grouped settings; reduced-motion preference; release details and Ctrl+K command palette. Existing controls and action handlers are retained.
validation: 105 existing Python tests passed. Isolated browser checks cover all 13 pages at 1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3840x2160, 1280x800 and 720x640; no page-level horizontal overflow or JavaScript errors. Settings category navigation, original element IDs, palette keyboard task opening, memory search and task filters passed. Native verification and scope limits are recorded in review/visual-overhaul/VALIDATION.md. Live providers, native audio and every external action were not tested.

title: Conversational briefings with expandable evidence
summary: Briefing replies and voice replay use natural sentences and up to three headlines. Raw links, repeated timestamps and technical source records are kept in expandable on-screen details. Existing voice provider remains unchanged. Missing data and older headlines are still labelled.
validation: 42 Python checks passed. Browser coverage checks conversational reply text and expandable evidence. Native voice audibility not tested. Expanded details are delivered for the current response; older chat history retains the conversational text only.

title: Integrated desktop header and bold JARVIS heading
summary: Windows uses a hidden native title bar with matching dark window-control overlay. The application header provides a draggable region with clickable navigation and reserved space for native minimise, maximise and close controls. JARVIS heading uses bold weight 800.
validation: Desktop JavaScript syntax checks passed. Electron documented hidden-title-bar and native overlay APIs used. Requires desktop restart; native dragging and caption controls have not yet been runtime-tested.

title: Fresh briefing evidence and bounded action receipts
summary: Daily briefings read outstanding tasks, reminders and the actual project registry. Each section reports check time, empty/failure/stale states and coverage. Common unsupported action-completion phrases are replaced with actual current-request receipts. Evidence notes include failure and check times. Simple briefings bypass chat-model inference.
validation: 42 offline Python checks and one isolated Chrome UI test passed; Python and JavaScript syntax checks passed. Chrome used real backend-generated fixture events with external providers mocked. Live Electron loading, news services and native speech were not tested. Completion-claim checks are bounded patterns, not universal fact verification.

title: Desktop backup access corrected
summary: Completed backups are copied into a new sibling file before publication, inheriting the backup folder's existing permissions. Moving a ZIP out of an owner-only temporary folder had preserved Codex-only access. No ACLs or Windows security settings are changed. Verification uses temporary storage beside the archive and errors identify the rehearsal stage.
validation: 14 recovery/HTTP checks passed. The old archive's ACL excluded the desktop user; the replacement inherited user access. Replacement backup 50fe5f453d084b32aec90bad88b4edd0 (3:56:25 PM, 164 files) passed restore rehearsal through the running Electron desktop UI. File hashes, SQLite integrity and table counts matched; restored code and hardware were not executed/tested.

title: Recovery failure diagnostics
summary: Recovery errors now show the failed operation and exception code without exposing private exception text. This improves diagnosis of the reported desktop restore failure; it does not establish its cause or fix it.
validation: 12 recovery and HTTP checks passed. The existing real backup passed a fresh command-line rehearsal and an authenticated HTTP rehearsal. The user's desktop-only failure was not reproduced and needs a retry after loading this update.

title: Verified local backup and separate-folder recovery
summary: Settings can create a backup of the complete saved SQLite database, saved data folders and application source; verify every archived file; rehearse restoration; or recover into a new folder without overwriting the working app. API credentials, dependencies and downloaded model caches are excluded. Backups remain local and unencrypted. Update-history records now tolerate identical clock ticks.
validation: 38 offline Python checks passed, including backup, committed WAL data, corruption rejection, path checks, overwrite protection, authentication and update-history clock collisions. One isolated Chrome recovery-controls test and syntax checks passed. Recovered code execution, native devices and live cloud services were not tested. Real-backup rehearsal receipts are stored alongside backups.

title: Unified update history and service evidence checks
summary: Change History combines JARVIS proposals, curated release notes, and automatic local source snapshots. Main script fingerprints show whether loaded code matches disk. Service-status questions use actual session check records; a bounded guard replaces service-success claims with those records. Replies display tool-evidence scope.
validation: 47 offline Python tests, one isolated Chrome UI test, timer fast-path regression and JavaScript syntax checks passed. Model/service test-success claims covered by bounded deterministic checks. Native audio and live external services were not tested; this is not universal factual verification.

title: Timer replies retain the configured JARVIS voice
summary: Direct timer lookup avoids the chat model. Timer speech uses the configured provider and says when checked to account for synthesis delay.
validation: Timer-routing and speech-cancellation tests passed. User confirmed the earlier device-voice version gave correct time; the restored cloud voice was not independently heard by Codex.

title: Hologram and stop-command wording fixes
summary: Added enable hologram, show a hologram, and repeated stop phrases to narrow command routing.
validation: Automated command and cancellation checks passed. User reported hologram working; screenshot showed Stop talking acknowledged, but audio stopping was not independently measured.

title: Assistant capabilities package
summary: Installed 11 files adding inspection archive and improvement tracking, acknowledged controls, timer and memory management, and response timing records.
validation: Installation receipt verified all 11 reviewed files at installation. Subsequent edits change those hashes. Review and test evidence: review/capabilities-update. Not a certification of every feature.
